summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Two synthetic shift notes conflict on board revision (Rev C vs Rev D) and event count (three vs five); neither is shown to be authoritative and no vibration or retention data is attached, so no connector change can be supported yet.

anchors.excerpt: Controller board revision on the affected unit: Rev C.
Three J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
No vibration-test result or retention measurement is attached to this note.
Controller board revision on the affected unit: Rev D.
Five J12 disconnect events were logged during vibration on the test track.
This note does not reference shift note A and does not explain the difference.
No vibration-test result or retention measurement is attached to this note.

knownFacts.statement: Shift note A records the controller board revision on the affected unit as Rev C.
Shift note A records three J12 disconnect events logged during vibration on the test track.
Shift note B records the controller board revision on the affected unit as Rev D.
Shift note B records five J12 disconnect events logged during vibration on the test track.
Shift note B does not reference shift note A and does not explain the difference.
Neither note has a vibration-test result or retention measurement attached.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate the current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 connector and investigate the root cause of the logged disconnects (e.g., mating, retention, cable strain) on the confirmed board revision. Inference: root cause is unknown; no evidence shows the connector itself is at fault.
prerequisites: Reconcile which board revision (Rev C or Rev D) the affected unit actually uses
Reconcile the event count (three vs five) against raw logs
Obtain a vibration profile and retention measurement for the current J12 installation

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement J12 connector
alternatives.description: Evaluate a replacement connector that preserves the existing board pinout and drive controller board footprint (author-entered constraint from the brief). Compatibility of any replacement is unknown until evidenced; no candidate part is named in the sources.
prerequisites: Confirm the authoritative board revision and its J12 footprint
Define the vibration environment and retention requirement
Show pinout and footprint compatibility with physical evidence before any change approval

evidenceGaps.gap: Conflict: note A states Rev C, note B states Rev D for the affected unit's controller board; neither is established as authoritative.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: The baseline is unknown; footprint, pinout and any change evaluation depend on the actual board revision.

evidenceGaps.gap: Conflict: note A records three disconnect events, note B records five; note B does not explain the difference.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Event frequency affects severity assessment and whether the notes describe the same unit or period.

evidenceGaps.gap: No vibration-test result or retention measurement is attached to either note; no vibration profile was supplied.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without measurements there is no basis to attribute disconnects to the connector or to judge any replacement.

evidenceGaps.gap: No current J12 part number, rating or candidate replacement is identified in the sources; the constraint source SYN-REQ-v1 is not in the frozen manifest.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Compatibility with the preserved pinout and footprint cannot be checked.

reviewQuestions.question: Which board revision (Rev C or Rev D) is actually fitted to the affected unit, as shown by physical inspection or build records?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Access to the unit or its build/serial records

reviewQuestions.question: Do notes A and B describe the same unit and time window, and what do the raw event logs show for the disconnect count?
What vibration profile and retention requirement apply to J12 on the test track?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Vibration profile and retention measurement plan

reviewQuestions.question: What evidence must exist before any connector change is approved, given the pinout and footprint must be preserved?

nextAction.action: Physically confirm the controller board revision on the affected unit and reconcile both shift notes against raw event logs before evaluating any connector change.
nextAction.requiredInput: Unit inspection or build record showing board revision; raw J12 disconnect logs

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
All sources are labeled synthetic fixtures invented for demonstration; statements are tagged kind "synthetic fixture".
The pinout/footprint constraint is author-entered from the brief; its referenced source SYN-REQ-v1 is not in the frozen manifest and was not reviewed.
No record is selected as authoritative; the conflicts are recorded as evidence gaps.
